title: Dual-contract opponent-seat gradient-conflict audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The residual PPO failures arise from incompatible opponent-seat policy gradients that a scalar mixed loss averages into regressions; a deterministic conflict-aware aggregate may expose a common descent direction unavailable to global or group-RMS normalization.
material_change: Reconstruct the immutable 4,096-hand group-RMS training cohort at the exact frozen zero-residual policy, compute six opponent-seat policy-gradient vectors with within-group centered/RMS advantages, audit pairwise cosine and group directional derivatives for the ordinary mean versus a deterministic conflict-aware aggregate. No training, checkpoint mutation, evaluation reuse for selection, or new environment hands.
baseline: Group-RMS matched treatment improved only Slumbot-free (+7.273 bb/100), regressed Standard10 (-6.250) and CFR96 (-2.535), pooled -0.504 CI[-16.184,15.176]. Standard10 remains the only reproducible mature frontier parent; imitation fresh20k -18.5025 and prior solver/regret routes are negative controls.
notes: Admission to a trained matched smoke requires material gradient conflict (at least two pairwise cosines below -0.10 or a mean aggregate that is locally harmful to at least one group) and a deterministic conflict-aware aggregate with strictly positive gradient alignment for all six groups and a better worst-group normalized alignment than the ordinary mean. This audit does not use the prior evaluation outcomes for optimization.

The exact preregistered command completed gradient computation and wrote raw/NPZ artifacts, then failed before summary creation because NumPy scalar gate counts were not JSON serializable. Preserved the first-attempt artifacts under run_serialization_failure_20260901T1334; fixed only scalar conversion and will rerun the same evidence/seed.

The serialization-fixed run completed but failed the preregistered initial-residual identity gate (cd37de89 versus parent f0888035). Root cause: the parent loaded three opponent modules before residual initialization, consuming Torch RNG. Preserved this non-comparable output under run_initial_state_mismatch_20260901T1336; added the same explicit opponent-load sequence and exact corrected command. No evidence or selection gate changed.

Exact-parent recovery loaded all three opponent modules before residual initialization and matched parent initial residual SHA f0888035682556bfee647ed57a28ae2d3c66578e26192bb84a1e69b79329fbce. The earlier non-comparable and serialization-failure artifacts remain quarantined and registered.

result.summary: Exact-parent reconstruction of 9,026 policy decisions found material opponent-seat gradient conflict: four pairwise cosines were below -0.10 (minimum -0.3362), and the ordinary decision-weighted aggregate had negative alignment -0.1708 for one of six groups. A deterministic minimum-norm convex combination produced strictly positive alignment for all six groups with worst alignment +0.5039.
result.conclusion: The local mechanism is real on this frozen cohort: scalar group-RMS aggregation can actively harm one opponent-seat objective even though rescaling advantages alone was correct. Conflict-aware aggregation supplies a mathematically valid common descent direction at the exact parent state. This establishes implementation/training-smoke value, not poker-strength efficacy or a scale claim.
result.next_step: Run one offline matched training smoke on the immutable cohort with identical sampled group batches and shared value/entropy updates, changing only ordinary versus minimum-norm policy-gradient aggregation; evaluate both frozen arms on untouched common decks. Interpret non-significance as insufficient evidence unless mechanism or broad direction clearly fails.
